name: IAIA Museum of Contemporary Native Arts
funding: Part of IAIA (2023 revenue $30.1M); Congress appropriated $13.48M for Jul 2026-Sep 2027; Art Bridges and Ford Foundation grants to the museum.
watch: Tribal-college museum run by IAIA. The Trump FY2026 budget proposed closing IAIA, but the Senate funded it anyway.
records_note: Parent IAIA posts financial statements and a trustee list; ProPublica carries its Form 990s for 2012 to 2024; no annual report or donor list found.

name: Urban Shaman Contemporary Aboriginal Art
funding: Small artist-run centre; Canada Council gave $280k over two years (2017-18); also Manitoba Arts Council, Winnipeg Arts Council and Province of Manitoba.
watch: Indigenous artist-run centre founded in 1996 in the Exchange District.
records_note: T3010 returns sit on the CRA charity listing; the site names three directors and shows nine undated, unlabelled supporter logos; no annual reports.

name: Buku-Larrnggay Mulka Centre
funding: Small community art centre; core IVAIS support since 1998-99, plus NT Government, Ian Potter Foundation and Cotton On Foundation (retail).
watch: Yolŋu community-controlled art centre, founded 1976. A local landowner corporation that earns bauxite royalties gave money in 2017.
records_note: ACNC holds annual reports for 2017 and 2018 and financial reports for 2013 to 2025; the centre's own site lists no funders or board.

name: Blak Dot Gallery
funding: Very small First Nations artist-run space; Australian Government Indigenous Languages and Arts, Creative Victoria and Merri-bek Council.
watch: First Nations-led gallery in Brunswick, founded in 2011. Hosted the 2014 '18C' protest show against Racial Discrimination Act changes.
records_note: ACNC holds financial reports for 2021 to 2026; the about page names three government funders, undated; no annual reports and no named board.

name: Sámi Center for Contemporary Art (Sámi Dáiddaguovddáš)
funding: 2025 revenue NOK 7.9M; Sámi Parliament direct grant NOK 6.09M (2025), plus Troms og Finnmark county.
watch: Sámi contemporary art centre, founded 1986, a foundation since 2013. The director and several board members changed over 2025-26.
records_note: Audited accounts for 2023 to 2025 are in Norway's accounts register; the site lists the full board but no annual reports or funders.

name: Toi Māori Aotearoa
funding: Small charitable trust; major funder is Creative New Zealand (government and Lotteries money); runs the Toi Māori Gallery.
watch: Māori arts trust and artists' network founded in 1996; mainly a service body with a small gallery and shop.
records_note: Annual reports 2018 to 2025 carry financial statements; the 2025 report names Creative New Zealand as core funder with partner acknowledgements and lists the trustees.

name: Foam Fotografiemuseum Amsterdam
funding: Small photo museum (193k visitors 2019); City of Amsterdam, tickets, VriendenLoterij, VandenEnde Foundation, Garanti BBVA International (bank), Deutsche Börse Photography Foundation.
watch: Roster read via a Dec 2025 archive of its partnerships page; a lottery and a bank are the corporate names to know.
records_note: Annual reports for 2024 and 2025 carry the accounts, named funders and the supervisory board; an undated partnerships page names four major partners.

name: Fotomuseum Winterthur
funding: City of Winterthur gives CHF 738k a year for 2025-2032; also Canton of Zurich, Verein, Volkart Stiftung, Ringier, Monterosa and about 20 foundations.
watch: Name to know: the Krupp foundation, a funder that holds 10% of warship builder TKMS and 21% of thyssenkrupp.
records_note: Annual reports 2019 to 2024 include accounts and named partners and patrons; the Stiftungsrat is named on the About page.

name: Jeu de Paume
funding: €8.6M budget in 2024, 68% from the Ministry of Culture; Jaeger-LeCoultre, CHANEL, Fondation Neuflize OBC, Louis Roederer and Swiss Life also fund it.
watch: 2013 censorship row: after a complaint from the CRIF, the culture ministry made it add visitor notices to Ahlam Shibli's show.
records_note: Activity reports 2019 to 2025 are posted, but without financial statements; the patrons page shows undated logos, and the governance page lists the association's members.

name: International Center of Photography
funding: About $8M revenue and $15M expenses (FY2023 Form 990); corporate supporters are Fondation d'entreprise Hermès, Select Equity, Harlowe, Paramount Global, MPB and Hearst.
watch: 2020 open letter from about 150 community members over students' protest photos; ICP refused to make students take them down.
records_note: Form 990s for 2021 to 2024 are posted on its site and in ProPublica; corporate supporters show as undated logos, and the board is listed.

name: Ars Electronica Center
funding: Over 170k visitors in 2024; City of Linz and Linz AG (municipal utility) as core partners, with Siemens, KUKA, Land Oberösterreich, Dorotheum and ORF.
watch: Bloomberg Philanthropies, an excluded name, is a current project partner on the Center's partners page.
records_note: It posts no annual report; accounts are filed in the Austrian company register, partners show as logos, and an advisory board is named.

name: Almaty Museum of Arts
funding: Opened 12 Sep 2025 for about US$100M (building and collection); Astana Motors (cars, malls) pays running costs, and Halyk Bank has been Lead Partner since Mar 2026.
watch: Private museum of Nurlan Smagulov. Its lead bank partner is majority-owned by Nazarbayev's son-in-law Timur Kulibayev.
records_note: Targeted-use-of-funds reports for 2021 to 2024 are posted; the partners page names only Halyk Bank, undated; the team page lists staff, not a board.
